alt: An email from Wells Fargo Online notifying the recipient that their dispute regarding an Uber transaction has been closed and a temporary credit of $32.91 has been made permanent.
summary:
This document is an email from "Wells Fargo Online" with the subject line "Wells Fargo: Your dispute is closed." The email, dated Monday, May 25, 2026, at 12:31 AM, informs the recipient that their dispute has been resolved and a temporary credit of $32.91, posted on April 7, 2026, is now permanent. The dispute details indicate a transaction with "UBER *TRIP" for $32.91, posted on February 10, 2026, with the status "Credit is Permanent."

Legally, this email serves as official notification from Wells Fargo regarding the resolution of a financial dispute. It confirms that the cardholder is no longer liable for the disputed amount and that the credit is permanent. The email also advises that a notation may appear on the next billing statement, which will be removed after the statement period closes, ensuring no finance charges or fees are applied to the disputed transaction.

A significant discrepancy is observed in the dates provided. The email itself is dated May 25, 2026, the dispute was posted on February 10, 2026, and the temporary credit was applied on April 7, 2026. All these dates are in the future relative to the current year (2024), which strongly suggests the document is either a simulated or fabricated email, or a test communication, rather than a genuine historical record. The sender's email address, `alerts_at_notify.wellsfargo.com`, appears legitimate for Wells Fargo notifications, but the future dates raise serious questions about the document's authenticity as a real-world transaction record.
